newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Aug palm oil output seen up 5-10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Aug palm oil output seen up 5-10 pct.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil output in August is estimated to have risen between five to 10 percent over July, plantation houses said on Thursday.

"The rise was attributed to the seasonal uptrend in production," said a dealer at a plantation firm said, adding that output in the east Malaysian state of Sabah was picking up after a slight drop in yields in July.
Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong said in a recent report that continuing good harvests in leading producing areas were likely in September and October.
Palm oil output normally peaks in October.
Weather conditions remained favourable with frequent widespread showers and occasional thunderstorms, Wong added.
He has projected output to rise by 11 percent to 801,000 tonnes in August from July. He is expected to release his final August palm oil output/stock/export estimates on Friday.
Official Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) data are due on September 16.
Traders had estimated palm oil stocks at end-August at 780,000-790,000 tonnes compared with PORLA's 754,634 at end-July.
Exports in August were estimated at 670,000-690,000 tonnes against PORLA's 646,017 tonnes in July.
